courses.name: Personal & Professional Development
courses.currentEvidence: Develops academic writing and research-literacy skills alongside personal development and civic engagement. Students locate and evaluate scholarly sources, synthesize literature, formulate research questions and arguments, and construct a research-paper introduction. A community-engaged project with a societal partner connects these skills to collaboration, reflection and practical contribution. Personal development planning addresses learning goals, self-efficacy, and stress and time management; the course also considers responsible academic use of AI.
courses.methods: Scholarly literature searching and source evaluation; Literature synthesis; CARS model for research introductions; Reflective development planning; Community project co-design
courses.finding: Direct subject/method contribution to comparativeliterary,cultural,historical,linguistic/media analysis; relevance assessed at completeprogrammeweight, not automaticallyFrench-specific.

courses.name: Modern History
courses.currentEvidence: Surveys economic, political and cultural developments from 1815 to the present while questioning the meaning and periodization of modernity. Students examine industrialization, political ideologies, nationalism, imperialism, migration, world wars, revolution, decolonization, the Cold War and globalization. Historical research and essays connect specific questions to evidence. A group project analyzes historical visions of the future as products of their own contexts and compares them with subsequent developments.
courses.methods: Historical contextualization; Primary- and secondary-source analysis; Source triangulation; Historical research-question development
courses.finding: Direct subject/method contribution to comparativeliterary,cultural,historical,linguistic/media analysis; relevance assessed at completeprogrammeweight, not automaticallyFrench-specific.

courses.name: History of Empires
courses.currentEvidence: Examines empires comparatively across global history, from ancient Persia, Rome and China to early-modern and modern imperial powers and contemporary claims to imperial status. Students analyze expansion, administration, military and economic systems, legitimacy, ideology, culture, decline and legacies. The course combines theories of empire with historically specific cases, historiographical discussion, source analysis and an independently developed research essay.
courses.methods: Comparative historical analysis; Historiographical analysis; Primary- and secondary-source analysis; Historical research-question development
courses.finding: Direct subject/method contribution to comparativeliterary,cultural,historical,linguistic/media analysis; relevance assessed at completeprogrammeweight, not automaticallyFrench-specific.

courses.name: Researching the “American Century”
courses.currentEvidence: Guides students through the full arc of historical inquiry, from formulating research questions to engaging critically with sources. Emphasises methodological rigour and interdisciplinary thinking and culminates in a substantial research paper.
courses.finding: Direct subject/method contribution to comparativeliterary,cultural,historical,linguistic/media analysis; relevance assessed at completeprogrammeweight, not automaticallyFrench-specific.

courses.name: European Union Politics
courses.currentEvidence: Studies EU institutions, political actors, integration and policymaking, linking formal rules to current political issues. Students analyze representation, legitimacy, interests, agenda setting, decision-making and implementation. A substantial empirical project examines European Parliament committee amendments, connecting MEP ideology and possible interest-group influence to amendment activity. Students develop a project plan, code amendments, assess salience and trace legislative processes.
courses.methods: EU policy and legislative-document research; Process tracing; Systematic amendment coding; Ideology and amendment-activity analysis; Salience assessment; Comparative news-source analysis
courses.finding: Direct subject/method contribution to comparativeliterary,cultural,historical,linguistic/media analysis; relevance assessed at completeprogrammeweight, not automaticallyFrench-specific.

courses.name: Introduction to Sociology
courses.currentEvidence: Introduces sociological reasoning through classical theories, their historical settings and perspectives that address exclusions from the discipline. Students connect solidarity, modernity, identity, social boundaries, networks and stratification to race, gender, migration and inequality in education and work. An individual analysis applies a course concept to contemporary social life without original data collection. A group paper develops a sociological question and analyzes a social problem using theory and academic literature.
courses.methods: Theory-guided sociological case analysis; Comparative analysis of sociological perspectives; Library-based social-science research; Sociological research-question formulation
courses.finding: Direct subject/method contribution to comparativeliterary,cultural,historical,linguistic/media analysis; relevance assessed at completeprogrammeweight, not automaticallyFrench-specific.

courses.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
courses.currentEvidence: Develops qualitative inquiry from research design and preparation through data collection, management, analysis and dissemination. Students examine methodological foundations, ethics, positionality and reflexivity alongside interviews, focus groups, ethnography, documentary and visual approaches. Coding, thematic interpretation and NVivo support analysis. Research teams formulate a question, collect and analyze qualitative evidence, and report their methodological decisions, findings and limitations in staged assignments.
courses.methods: Qualitative research design; Interviews; Focus groups; Ethnography and participant observation; Documentary and archival analysis; Visual-data analysis; Participatory video and drawing; Transcription; Qualitative coding; Thematic analysis; NVivo-supported analysis; Reflexive methodological evaluation
courses.finding: Direct subject/method contribution to comparativeliterary,cultural,historical,linguistic/media analysis; relevance assessed at completeprogrammeweight, not automaticallyFrench-specific.

courses.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
courses.currentEvidence: Focuses on civil society through critical, neo-functionalist and decolonial social theory. Students examine social trust, capital, hegemony, public spheres, solidarity, social movements and civil repair across political and regional contexts. An experience report relates personal engagement or observation to course concepts. An individual research project uses theoretical and empirical sources to analyze a civil-society organization, movement, initiative or related phenomenon.
courses.methods: Comparative social-theory analysis; Theory-guided empirical case analysis; Document and secondary-source analysis; Structured reflection on civil-society engagement or observation; Sociological research design
courses.finding: Direct subject/method contribution to comparativeliterary,cultural,historical,linguistic/media analysis; relevance assessed at completeprogrammeweight, not automaticallyFrench-specific.

courses.name: Psycholinguistics
courses.currentEvidence: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.
courses.finding: Direct subject/method contribution to comparativeliterary,cultural,historical,linguistic/media analysis; relevance assessed at completeprogrammeweight, not automaticallyFrench-specific.

courses.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
courses.currentEvidence: Introduces psychological and neuroscientific explanations of behaviour and mental processes. Students study neural signalling, brain anatomy and development, learning, intelligence, personality, social influence, mental disorders and treatments. Several sessions introduce behavioural, imaging and electrophysiological approaches to neuroscience and their combined use. Interdisciplinary research-article and case analysis connects psychological processes to neural mechanisms and clinical questions.
courses.methods: Psychological and neuroscientific research appraisal; Interdisciplinary case-study analysis
courses.finding: Direct subject/method contribution to comparativeliterary,cultural,historical,linguistic/media analysis; relevance assessed at completeprogrammeweight, not automaticallyFrench-specific.

courses.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication
courses.currentEvidence: Teaches rhetorical analysis and persuasive communication through classical history, theory and practice. Students study Greek and Roman rhetoric, the five canons, types of discourse, persuasive appeals, argumentation and fallacies. Written exercises, debates and public speeches develop invention, arrangement, style, memory and delivery. An applied project creates narrative and storytelling material for an immersive educational setting concerned with Zeeland's climate and community.
courses.methods: Rhetorical text analysis; Stasis analysis; Argument invention and arrangement; Stylistic analysis and composition; Structured debate; Persuasive speechwriting and delivery; Educational storytelling design
courses.finding: Direct subject/method contribution to comparativeliterary,cultural,historical,linguistic/media analysis; relevance assessed at completeprogrammeweight, not automaticallyFrench-specific.

courses.name: Style & Meaning
courses.currentEvidence: Studies how linguistic choices produce meaning and interpretive effects, principally in literary texts but also in nonfiction. Students connect linguistic description to interpretation across grammar, discourse and cognition. Stylistic frameworks address foregrounding, dialogue, narration, modality, transitivity, deixis, schemas, construal and text worlds. Frequent analysis exercises lead to an original, research-supported stylistic analysis of a selected text.
courses.methods: Linguistic stylistic analysis; Close textual analysis; Discourse and conversation analysis; Speech and thought presentation analysis; Modality and transitivity analysis; Deictic and cognitive-grammar analysis; Text-world analysis; Framework-based interpretation supported by retrievable textual evidence
courses.finding: Direct subject/method contribution to comparativeliterary,cultural,historical,linguistic/media analysis; relevance assessed at completeprogrammeweight, not automaticallyFrench-specific.

courses.name: Rhetoric in Action
courses.currentEvidence: Applies rhetoric through community-engaged work with local primary-school children. Students develop their own public-speaking, debating and storytelling skills, then design and iteratively refine age-appropriate teaching activities with school partners. On-site coaching and a final public-speaking event connect rhetorical education to civic participation and confidence. Structured reflection examines reciprocity, cultural sensitivity, personal development and the practical challenges of community-engaged teaching.
courses.methods: Public-speaking and debate coaching; Storytelling exercises; Iterative design and revision of teaching materials; Practice-based rhetorical instruction; Gibbs reflective-cycle analysis; Public-speaking event design and evaluation
courses.finding: Direct subject/method contribution to comparativeliterary,cultural,historical,linguistic/media analysis; relevance assessed at completeprogrammeweight, not automaticallyFrench-specific.

courses.name: Persuasive Communication
courses.currentEvidence: Examines contemporary persuasion through communication studies, social psychology and ethical analysis, then applies it in community-engaged work. Students study coactive persuasion, framing, argumentation, cognitive shortcuts and verbal and nonverbal communication. Projects with the Delta Climate Centre and Vlissingen municipality develop communication encouraging sustainable and circular lifestyles. An individual research paper evaluates selected persuasion tools through literature review, field research diaries and reflective analysis of their use.
courses.methods: Persuasive-message design; Communication consulting and implementation; Literature review; Qualitative research diaries; Action research; Reflective case-study analysis; Gibbs reflective cycle
courses.finding: Direct subject/method contribution to comparativeliterary,cultural,historical,linguistic/media analysis; relevance assessed at completeprogrammeweight, not automaticallyFrench-specific.

courses.name: Creative Communication Laboratory
courses.currentEvidence: Studies and develops creative communication through poetry, performance and critically articulated artistic practice. Students move from lyric foundations to constrained and experimental forms, attending to sound, rhythm, imagery, voice and embodiment. Close reading and creative workshops lead into an independent traditional or hybrid project grounded in scholarship and aesthetic traditions. Revision and reflection require students to justify formal, conceptual and procedural choices.
courses.methods: Close poetic reading and listening; Constraint-based composition; Poetic and performative experimentation; Structured drafting and revision; Critical analysis of creative decisions; Independent practice-based creative inquiry
courses.finding: Direct subject/method contribution to comparativeliterary,cultural,historical,linguistic/media analysis; relevance assessed at completeprogrammeweight, not automaticallyFrench-specific.

courses.name: African Art & Heritage
courses.currentEvidence: Introduces African art and heritage with particular attention to western African visual traditions and their cultural, religious and social meanings. Students study sculpture, masks and other forms across regional contexts before tracing African art's role in European modernism, the Harlem Renaissance and African artistic renewal. Colonial dispossession, museum collecting and restitution form a major later strand. An independent paper develops a research question supported by scholarly evidence.
courses.methods: Visual and contextual art-historical analysis; Comparative interpretation of artistic traditions; Analysis of primary artistic and critical texts; Heritage-restitution case analysis; Scholarly literature review and annotated bibliography; Independent art-historical research
courses.finding: Direct subject/method contribution to comparativeliterary,cultural,historical,linguistic/media analysis; relevance assessed at completeprogrammeweight, not automaticallyFrench-specific.

courses.name: Modern Art & Modern Museums
courses.currentEvidence: Examines modern and contemporary art from the late nineteenth century to the present together with the institutions that shape its display and reception. Students study avant-gardes, abstraction, modernist design, figuration, postmodern and conceptual practices, and global contemporary art. Museums, exhibitions, curatorial choices and Eurocentric narratives are treated critically. An independently researched paper develops a focused art-historical question, methods and evidence-based argument.
courses.methods: Art-historical interpretation and contextual analysis; Critical analysis of museums and curatorial practices; Scholarly literature review; Independent art-historical research
courses.finding: Direct subject/method contribution to comparativeliterary,cultural,historical,linguistic/media analysis; relevance assessed at completeprogrammeweight, not automaticallyFrench-specific.

courses.name: Writing Art's Histories
courses.currentEvidence: This course examines the history of art history as an academic discipline, tracing how scholars have understood and interpreted art from the sixteenth century to the present. Through critical readings of influential texts by figures such as Aby Warburg, Erwin Panofsky, Ernst Gombrich, Michel Foucault, and Jacques Derrida, students explore the major ideas and methodologies that have shaped the field. Topics include art and history, aesthetics, meaning and interpretation, authorship and identity, and the challenges of art history in a globalized world.
courses.finding: Direct subject/method contribution to comparativeliterary,cultural,historical,linguistic/media analysis; relevance assessed at completeprogrammeweight, not automaticallyFrench-specific.

courses.name: Introduction to Literary Studies
courses.currentEvidence: Introduces practical criticism and literary interpretation through fiction, poetry, drama and contemporary nonfiction, with an introductory component on film adaptation. Students investigate literary value and the constructed character of texts, using concepts of plot, character, setting, point of view, symbolism, style and form. Close reading and engagement with critical sources support analytical presentations and an essay or extended book review.
courses.methods: Close reading; Formalist literary analysis; Narrative analysis; Poetic and dramatic analysis; Critical-source integration; Literary essay and review construction
courses.finding: Direct subject/method contribution to comparativeliterary,cultural,historical,linguistic/media analysis; relevance assessed at completeprogrammeweight, not automaticallyFrench-specific.

courses.name: Great Literary Works
courses.currentEvidence: Surveys major literary works from ancient epic to modern and later fiction, connecting literary form to questions of humanity, mortality, gender, freedom, community and civilization. Students compare genres and recurring motifs through works including Gilgamesh, Greek tragedy, confessional writing, framed tales, philosophical satire, colonial narratives and modernist fiction. Text-focused analysis and engagement with criticism develop interpretation of theme, technique and cultural context.
courses.methods: Close literary reading; Formalist analysis of genre, theme and technique; Comparative textual interpretation; Narrative analysis; Critical-source interpretation and integration
courses.finding: Direct subject/method contribution to comparativeliterary,cultural,historical,linguistic/media analysis; relevance assessed at completeprogrammeweight, not automaticallyFrench-specific.

courses.name: World Myth & Literature
courses.currentEvidence: Compares mythic narratives across ancient and later literary traditions, examining transmission, cultural connections and themes of creation, power, gender, love and loyalty. Greek, Roman, Near Eastern, Indian, Arabic and African materials support comparisons of narrative patterns and representations. Students apply theories of myth and literary analysis in a research paper and graphic explanation, then creatively retell an Ovidian story using another cultural narrative model.

courses.currentEvidence: Studies documentary history, modes and styles alongside practical documentary production.
